note: Verify-first round against the 2026-08-14 external audit. Most of the audit's P0 surface was closed by the 2026-08 hardening rounds (docs/production-hardening-followups.md items 1-62); the items below are the residues a fresh sweep of HEAD confirmed as real. Full record: docs/production-hardening-plan.md section 9.

items.title: SQL: reject silently-dropped SELECT clauses (FOR UPDATE, FOR SHARE, SELECT INTO, bare HAVING, named WINDOW); global-or-refused LIMIT/OFFSET at parallelism > 1
items.risk: A query is accepted and returns numbers that do not mean what the SQL says.

items.title: Capabilities manifest: schema_version + git_sha/git_clean in --capabilities-json
items.risk: Tooling consuming the manifest cannot detect a schema change or map a manifest to a build.

items.title: HA: file-backend startup line states its per-host verification scope (etcd CAS + two-contender test verified already present)
items.risk: An operator reads split-brain safety into a backend that cannot provide it across hosts.

items.title: Compatibility inventory (docs/internals/protocol-compatibility.md) + frozen-bytes fixtures under tests/fixtures/
items.risk: An incompatible persistent format is consumed silently, or an encode/decode pair co-evolves past its own shipped artefacts.

items.title: DeterminismFacts populated from the job graph; UNKNOWN-vs-clean coverage semantics; surfaced wherever the guarantee report renders
items.risk: A delivery-exactly-once pipeline that replays to different values is reported as if replay-stable.

items.title: Real OTLP/HTTP export: metrics + lifecycle spans, --otlp-endpoint, no new dependency
items.risk: No production trace/metrics export path; the OTel boundary was a stub.

items.title: Tracking hygiene: W-table statuses reconciled with the follow-ups, round 9 recorded, planned-prs.json committed
items.risk: The plan doc misreports what CI proves - the exact staleness class the doc exists to catch.

items.title: Reusable source contract suite: a capability claim is a test obligation (public clink::test API; file family + parquet instantiated; caught and corrected parquet's stale non-replayable record)
items.risk: A connector's declared semantics drift from its implementation with nothing tying claim to behaviour; the guarantee analyser then reasons from fiction in either direction.
items.follow_up: per-impl rollout to the container-backed connectors under the live label

items.title: Reusable sink contract suite: the 2PC crash windows as capability-gated obligations (public clink::test API; file_2pc + parquet_2pc instantiated)
items.risk: A sink's exactly-once claim rests on crash windows nothing exercises uniformly: visible-before-commit, non-idempotent recommit, lost prepared transactions.

items.title: Contract suites live: postgres_2pc + s3_2pc under SinkContractSuite against real servers; new UpsertContractSuite (idempotency-key collapse) instantiated for postgres_upsert; Kafka exclusion documented (non-recoverable commit, KIP-939 the sanctioned future path)
items.risk: The 2PC crash windows were held hermetically but not against real PREPARE TRANSACTION / multipart-upload state; the effectively-once family had no executable collapse obligation at all.

items.title: Upsert contract rollout: redis_upsert, mysql_upsert, cassandra_upsert instantiated live; mongo exclusion documented (upsert is a mode on one factory whose record honestly claims at-least-once)
items.risk: Three connectors carried EffectivelyOnceIdempotent records with nothing holding the collapse behaviour behind the claim.
items.follow_up: changelog-delete semantics as an optional upsert-contract case; a mongo_upsert factory/op-type if the replace mode should be analyser-visible

items.title: Kafka prepared-transaction resume: wire-level FindCoordinator + EndTxn(commit) in-doubt resolution at HA restore-point selection, using pid/epoch captured from librdkafka's stats callback and staged in the checkpoint; CONFIRMED advances only on the broker's explicit acknowledgement
items.risk: A checkpoint completing whose broker commit had not executed when the worker died was the one window neither the sink nor the client could close; resolution commits the genuine orphan and advances the restore point past the interval, with the commit-confirmed bounded contract as the floor on every failure.
tests: TxnResumeWire/TxnResume (10, hermetic: byte-for-byte golden frame, parsers vs truncation/foreign correlation, fake broker: happy/fenced/unsupported/no-identity/unreachable, resolver through the registry)
ResolutionFixture (9: walk order, all-handles-must-commit, every conservative stop)
TxnResumeLive (3, real Redpanda: fork-crashed orphan committed exactly-once end to end, fenced identity refused, wrapper stages resolvable handle and erases on commit)
items.limitations: resolution runs on HA/lock-free recovery paths only (in-incarnation restarts keep the bounded contract until a lock-free restart phase exists); non-flexible protocol versions only (FindCoordinator v1/v2, EndTxn v1) and no SASL - both fall back, never guess; no single-run whole-chain HA e2e yet (each link is tested; the chain e2e is the named follow-up for the integration label). Revisit against librdkafka KIP-939 support when it ships.
